review.diagnosis: Migrated biliary stent lodged in a Meckel diverticulum, causing adjacent ileal perforation and purulent peritonitis.
review.reasoning: Operative exploration confirmed a biliary stent within a Meckel diverticulum approximately 40 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve, with its distal end perforating adjacent ileum. Purulent intraperitoneal fluid and adhesions were also documented. These findings explain the progressive abdominal pain, distension, nausea and peritoneal irritation. CT demonstrated small-bowel air–fluid levels and a linear intraluminal foreign body, supporting suspected mechanical obstruction, although its precise mechanism was not established. Migration from a prior biliary placement is the most likely etiological mechanism; the original placement, timing and migration route remain undocumented. The patient could not supply medication or exposure history. Blood tests were unavailable, and the returned CT report does not establish an angiographic assessment. Neither limitation weakens the directly observed perforation mechanism.
unconfirmed: Original biliary stent placement, indication and timing of migration
Definitive mechanical obstruction and its precise mechanism
next_steps: Complete urgent operative source control, including stent removal and treatment of the perforated bowel and involved diverticulum as indicated.
Provide intravenous antibiotics, resuscitation and postoperative monitoring; obtain blood count, renal function, electrolytes and lactate when available.
Review prior biliary procedure records to establish stent origin and assess any ongoing biliary management needs.
